documents.title: Compliances-Certificate under Reg. 74 (5) of SEBI (DP) Regulations, 2018
Shareholder Meeting / Postal Ballot-Outcome of AGM

analysis.summary: Shanti Gold reported its Q1 FY27 earnings with strong revenue and profit growth driven by volume expansion and the commencement of its Marol manufacturing facility. Management maintains its top-line guidance of 50% to 60% value growth and 30% to 40% volume growth for the year, while projecting sustainable EBITDA margins of 7.5% to 8%. The company is executing a rights issue of up to INR100 crores to support working capital and capacity expansion, including an upcoming facility in Jaipur. Management remains highly optimistic about organized jewellery demand and long-term gold market fundamentals. Shanti Gold International Limited reported its financial and operational performance for Q1 FY27 and FY26, highlighting significant revenue and volume growth supported by capacity expansion.

guidance.claim: Management guides for 50% to 60% growth in top-line value and 30% to 40% growth in volume for the current year.
guidance.quote: And the top line, we stick to our guidance of around 50% to 60% growth this year. So, if I have to go for the volume and the value, volume will remain largely in the 30% to 40% range and the value will remain in the 50% to 60% range as compared to last year.

guidance.claim: Management expects around 30% to 40% growth in terms of volume and around 60% to 70% growth in terms of value for the coming year.
guidance.quote: So this year, i.e current coming year, it will be around 30% to 40% growth in terms of volume and around 60%-70% growth in terms of value

guidance.claim: Management stated that the core PAT margin business model margin would be around 4% plus.
guidance.quote: This margin would be around 4% and all, which we've been maintaining that 4% plus and all.

guidance.claim: Management expects export contribution to increase from 10% to 20% or more.
guidance.quote: So I told you like this year will be like from 5% to we are going to go up to 10% or maybe more. Sorry, from 10% to 20%.

demand_outlook.claim: Management states that the outlook for organized jewellery continues to be constructive, supported by wedding and occasion-led demand and rising disposable incomes.
demand_outlook.quote: From an industry perspective, the outlook for the organized jewellery continues to remain constructive. India's jewellery market is supported by strong wedding and occasion-led demand, rising disposable incomes, and an increasable preference for organized and branded jewellery.

demand_outlook.claim: Growing disposable income drives gold as a status symbol and investment.
demand_outlook.quote: Growing disposable income drives gold as status symbol & investment

demand_outlook.claim: Seasonal demand arises from weddings, Diwali, and harvest festivals.
demand_outlook.quote: Seasonal demand from weddings, Diwali & harvest festivals

demand_outlook.claim: Unique Indian designs attract global buyers, providing export growth potential.
demand_outlook.quote: Unique Indian designs attracting global buyers; export growth potential

demand_outlook.claim: Branded players are driving consumer trust in the jewellery market.
demand_outlook.quote: Branded players (Tanishq, Kalyan, Malabar) driving consumer trust

demand_outlook.claim: Demand trends remained resilient across key markets and customer segments despite elevated gold prices during the year.
demand_outlook.quote: Despite elevated gold prices during the year, overall demand trends remained resilient across key markets and customer segments.

demand_outlook.claim: The company continues to witness healthy transactions, particularly in wedding and occasions-led jewellery categories.
demand_outlook.quote: We continue to witness healthy transactions, particularly in wedding and occasions-led jewellery categories.

demand_outlook.claim: The increasing outsourcing preference among organized jewellers and retailers is a structural shift benefiting the company.
demand_outlook.quote: One of the most encouraging trends we are witnessing today is the increasing outsourcing preference among organized jewellers, retailers, as retailers continue to focus on expanding their footprint, inventory optimizing, and faster design cycles.

capex_expansion.claim: The company has approved a rights issue of 46,43,471 equity shares aggregating up to INR100 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: As part of our growth and capital planning, the company has approved a rights issue of 46,43,471 fully paid-up equity shares of face value 10 each, aggregating up to INR100 crores.

capex_expansion.claim: The Jaipur facility is allotted a capex of around INR47 crores and is expected to be operational around mid-November or December.
capex_expansion.quote: So capex is around INR47 crores what we have allotted for Jaipur facility, and it should be operational around November, mid-November or December, because the factory work is still going on.

capex_expansion.claim: The upcoming Jaipur facility is spread across 3 acres of land, with the initial 50,000 square feet representing the first phase of commencement.
capex_expansion.quote: Jaipur factory is actually spread across 3 acres of land, and this 50,000 is just one segment of those, of the whole plant that we have.

capex_expansion.claim: The new Marol facility in Mumbai will add approximately 4,000 kilo per annum of manufacturing capacity.
capex_expansion.quote: our new Marol facility in Mumbai, which will add approximately 4,000 kilo per annum of manufacturing capacity.

capex_expansion.claim: The 1,200 kilo per annum capacity addition announced during an IPO at Jaipur continues to progress in line with expectations.
capex_expansion.quote: In addition, the 1,200 kilo per annum capacity addition announced during an IPO at Jaipur, continues to progress in line with expectations.

capex_expansion.claim: The new Marol facility is expected to start in a month or so, and the Jaipur factory should start by around September or October.
capex_expansion.quote: So see, our new factory is almost ready, which is going to be like in a month or so for Marol factory, and I guess Jaipur factory should be starting by around September, October now.

capex_expansion.claim: Capacity additions will take the total installed manufacturing capacity to nearly 7,900 kilogram per annum.
capex_expansion.quote: Once operational, this addition will take our total installed manufacturing capacity to nearly 7,900 kilogram per annum, positioning us strongly for the next phase of scalable growth.

margins_costs.claim: Sustainable EBITDA margins are expected to be around 7.5% to 8% going forward.
margins_costs.quote: So roughly 2% to 2.5% was the inventory gain. So if you remove that percent, roughly going forward, looking at the current demand and all, we should be in the range of 7.5% to 8% EBITDA.

margins_costs.claim: Q1 EBITDA margin was elevated by roughly 2% to 2.5% due to unrealized gains locked in finished goods inventory from the previous year following a change in inventory valuation method from FIFO to WAC.
margins_costs.quote: See, basically, a part of the margin has spilled over from the unrealized gain locked in the finished goods of last year. See, there was a change in inventory method from FIFO to WAC method. There was some unrealized gain which was locked in the inventory of last year, which got spilled in this current year.

margins_costs.claim: Gross profit for Q1 FY27 stood at ₹78.0 crore with a gross margin of 10.9%.
EBITDA for Q1 FY27 was ₹71.5 crore, resulting in an EBITDA margin of 10.0%.
Profit After Tax (PAT) for Q1 FY27 was ₹50.5 crore with a PAT margin of 7.1%.
EBITDA margins for Q4 FY26 stood at 10.17% compared to 7.10% in the corresponding period last year, improving by 306 basis points.
margins_costs.quote: EBITDA margins for the quarter stood at 10.17% as compared to 7.10% in the corresponding period last year, improving by 306 basis points.

margins_costs.claim: EBITDA margins for FY26 stood at 9.86% compared to 8.13% in FY25, improving by 173 basis points.
margins_costs.quote: EBITDA margins for FY26 stood at 9.86% as compared to 8.13% in FY25, improving by 173 basis points.

margins_costs.claim: PAT margins for FY26 stood at 6.94% compared to 4.89% in FY25, improving by 205 basis points Y-o-Y.
margins_costs.quote: PAT margins for FY26 stood at 6.94% as compared to 4.89% in FY25, improving by 205 basis pointsY-o-Y.

orders_capacity.claim: Current capacity utilization at the Mumbai manufacturing facility stands at 75%.
Export revenue accounted for 4% of total revenue in Q1.
orders_capacity.quote: Basically in Q1, Q1, our export still pertains to 4% of the total revenue.

orders_capacity.claim: The existing Andheri manufacturing facility has an installed capacity of approximately 2,700 kilo per annum.
orders_capacity.quote: Our existing Andheri manufacturing facility with an installed capacity of approximately 2,700 kilo per annum has been operating at healthy utilization levels in line with the growth of our new Marol facility in Mumbai

orders_capacity.claim: The company's present capacity utilization is around 65%.
The company serves more than 400 customers.

capital_allocation.claim: The company maintains a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.50 and plans to keep it below 1x.
capital_allocation.quote: See, debt-to-equity, madam, currently we are at 0.50, which is still – we plan to go up to less than one maybe because still, as I told you, we are on a growth spree.

capital_allocation.claim: Proceeds from the rights issue will be invested completely in gold and working capital.
capital_allocation.quote: So right now we -- the money what we are acquiring from rights issue is going to be invested completely in gold and working capital.

capital_allocation.claim: Management stated that the company is comfortable going up to a debt-equity ratio of 1:1 to fuel future growth expansion.
capital_allocation.quote: To answer your question, maximum at this point if I say, we should be comfortable at going at 1:1. That's what we are aiming for now to fuel the future growth expansion.

risks_headwinds.claim: The incorporation timeline for the Dubai subsidiary has been extended due to geopolitical situations and ongoing wars.
risks_headwinds.quote: So due to all these wars and all, it is extended for a couple of months more ahead now because the situation, geopolitical things are not good.

management_commitments.claim: The company expects the Jaipur facility to commence operations around mid-November or December.
management_commitments.quote: So capex is around INR47 crores what we have allotted for Jaipur facility, and it should be operational around November, mid-November or December, because the factory work is still going on.

management_commitments.claim: Management maintains its full-year guidance for 50% to 60% value growth and 30% to 40% volume growth.
management_commitments.quote: So, if I have to go for the volume and the value, volume will remain largely in the 30% to 40% range and the value will remain in the 50% to 60% range as compared to last year.

management_commitments.claim: The company transitioned its inventory valuation methodology from FIFO to weighted average cost with retrospective effect from April 01, 2024.
management_commitments.quote: The company has transitioned its inventory valuation methodology from the First In, First Out, FIFO method to the weighted average cost WAC method with retrospective effect from April 01, 2024.

management_commitments.claim: The Marol factory will initially start at around 100 kgs per month and reach up to 4,000 kilos very soon.
management_commitments.quote: So initially to start with, like I expect this Marol factory initially few months to start with, it's going to be around 100 kgs per month and reaching very soon we'll be reaching till 4,000 kilos.

management_commitments.claim: The Jaipur factory is expected to start by around September or October.
management_commitments.quote: and I guess Jaipur factory should be starting by around September, October now.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
